title: 树荫下的公园长椅  (The Shaded Park Bench)

segments.t: Under leafy trees at the quiet public garden at the end of Wutong Lane, Qing, Hao, and Manager Zhou gather around a green wooden park bench to read the fourth and final watercolour card. Let us listen in first.
啊，树荫底下舒服的木头长椅——我的脚太满意第四张线索了！
听最后一句小诗：坐在树荫下，把四个角一起带回家。
把四个角合在一起……小晴，快把一、二、三号卡片递给我！
等等——看每张卡片外边画着的淡蓝线！
把背面翻上来，像正方形的四块瓷砖一样平铺在长椅木条上……
一号左上，二号右上，三号左下，四号右下！
天哪！四张背面合起来，居然是小院客栈的鸟瞰图！
这儿是院子里的老树，那儿是九号房的拱窗……
再看二楼院子的木头阳台——上面画了一颗鲜红的星！
那位制图员为什么在我们楼上的阳台画一颗红星呢？！
小晴，说不定答案就在你口袋里那个火漆小信封里面！
每条线索我们都老老实实走完了——连周经理多绕的那一圈也算——快拆开吧！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
啊，树荫底下舒服的木头长椅——我的脚太满意第四张线索了！
'Ah, a comfortable wooden bench in the shade—my feet approve of Clue Four!' "Shuyin" combines "tree" and "shade" for cool leafy shadow, and "manyi" means thoroughly pleased or satisfied.
听最后一句小诗：坐在树荫下，把四个角一起带回家。

'Listen to the final rhyme: Sit in the shade and bring all four corners home together.' "Xiaoshi" literally means a "little poem" or short clue rhyme, and "dai huijia" links "bring" straight to "home".
把四个角合在一起……小晴，快把一、二、三号卡片递给我！
'Bring all four corners together... hand me Cards One, Two, and Three, Qing!' "Di gei wo" means "pass to me" from hand to hand, while "he zai yiqi" joins separate pieces together.
等等——看每张卡片外边画着的淡蓝线！
'Wait—look at the faint blue lines drawn along the outer edges of each card!' Pairing "dan", "pale", with "lan", "blue", gives "faint blue", and "waibian" names the outer edge of each card.
把背面翻上来，像正方形的四块瓷砖一样平铺在长椅木条上……

'Turn them face up on the flat bench slat like four tiles of one square...' "Xiang... yiyang" frames "just like...", while "zhengfangxing" names an even four-sided square built from four "cizhuan", tiles.
一号左上，二号右上，三号左下，四号右下！

'Card One top left, Card Two top right, Card Three bottom left, Card Four bottom right!' grid corners in Mandarin put "left" or "right" first and "shang", top, or "xia", bottom, second: "zuo shang" is top left.
天哪！四张背面合起来，居然是小院客栈的鸟瞰图！
'Incredible! Together the four backs form a bird-eye drawing of Courtyard Inn!' "Niaokantu" literally says "bird-look-down picture"—a spot-on match for an overhead bird-eye view!
这儿是院子里的老树，那儿是九号房的拱窗……
'There is our courtyard tree, there are the arched windows of Room Nine...' "Gongchuang" joins "arch" and "window" for the curved sunroom windows, echoing the bookshop's "gongmen", arched doorway.
再看二楼院子的木头阳台——上面画了一颗鲜红的星！
'And look up on the second-floor wooden courtyard balcony—a bright red painted star!' Stars and pearls take the counter "ke", while "yangtai" literally pairs "sun" and "terrace" for an open balcony.
那位制图员为什么在我们楼上的阳台画一颗红星呢？！

'Why did the mapmaker paint a red star on our upstairs courtyard balcony?!' Respectful "wei" counts people politely in "na wei zhituyuan", "that mapmaker", and final "ne" sharpens the puzzled question.
小晴，说不定答案就在你口袋里那个火漆小信封里面！
'Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, Qing!' "Shuobuding" literally says "cannot say for sure"—a breezy spoken "perhaps"—and "huoqi" means sealing wax.
每条线索我们都老老实实走完了——连周经理多绕的那一圈也算——快拆开吧！

'We walked every clue honestly—even Manager Zhou and his extra circle—so let us open it!' "Laolaoshishi" doubles both syllables of "laoshi", "honest", for "fair and square", while "lian... ye" means "even... too".
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

Placed edge to edge on the shaded park bench, the four cards unite into a secret map of Courtyard Inn crowned with a bright red star. See you next time.
